get.description: Returns up to 20 customers per call in `customers`. `pagination` gives you `total`, the number of customers across all pages; `has_next`, which is `true` when there is another page; and `next_page`, the URL of that page. Parameter names are case-sensitive. An unknown or wrongly cased name, such as `firstName`, `max` or `postcode`, is rejected with `400 unknown_parameter`, and `errors[0]` in the response names the parameter. `createdFrom`, `createdTo`, `updatedFrom` and `updatedTo` are accepted but ignored: they do not narrow the results. Listed customers do not include `custom_properties`; to get them, use [Retrieve a customer](/api-reference/customers/retrieve-a-customer).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of customers per page, up to `20`. A larger value is treated as `20`; `pagination.limit` shows the value used.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of customers to skip. If you send both `offset` and `page`, `offset` is used.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at `1`. Each page holds `limit` customers.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text search. You can also send it as `searchText`, `query` or `keyword`.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Filters customers by email address.

parameters.name: companyName
parameters.description: Filters customers by company name.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: Filters customers by phone number.

parameters.name: mobile
parameters.description: Filters customers by mobile number.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Filters customers by country.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filters customers by state.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: Filters customers by city.

parameters.name: postCode
parameters.description: Filters customers by post code. The name is case-sensitive: `postcode` is rejected with `400 unknown_parameter`.

parameters.name: customerGroup
parameters.description: Filters customers by customer group.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Returns only customers with this status: `active`, `inactive`, `pending`, `approval_awaiting` or `awaiting_verification`. Letter case does not matter. Any other value is rejected with `400`, and the error message lists the allowed values.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort the results by. An unknown field is rejected with `400 invalid_sort_field`.

200.description: `customers` holds up to `limit` customers, and `pagination` holds `total`, `has_next` and `next_page`.

400.description: Rejected because a parameter name is unknown or wrongly cased (`unknown_parameter`), the `sort` field is unknown (`invalid_sort_field`), or `status` is not one of the five allowed values.

x-codeSamples.source:

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN"

post.description: Creates a customer from the fields you send in the `customer` object and returns `201` with the new customer. Use its `customer_id`, not its `internal_id`, in later calls. `first_name` is required. `status` must be `active`, `inactive`, `pending`, `approval_awaiting` or `awaiting_verification`. If you leave `status` out, the API creates the customer as `awaiting_verification` with no usable password, even if you sent one. For that customer, [Change a password](/api-reference/customers/change-a-password) returns `401`, even straight after [Reset a password](/api-reference/customers/reset-a-password). To create a customer who can sign in, send `status: "active"` together with `password`. To create a company, send `company: true` and `company_name`. The response includes `company_name` but not `company`. The API accepts address fields placed directly on the customer, such as `address1`, `suburb` and `postcode`, but does not save them. To save addresses, use [Add addresses](/api-reference/customers/add-addresses). The response always lists three addresses, `primary`, `shipping` and `billing`, even when you sent none. If no address was saved, all three are blank. `primary` and `billing` share one `id`, so they are one saved address.

201.description: The customer was created. Returns the new customer in `customer`, including its `customer_id`.

400.description: The request is invalid. For example, a missing `first_name` returns the message `Customer name is required`.

409.description: Another customer already uses this email address. This includes deleted customers. The message is `Provided email already registered`.

put.description: Updates a customer and returns `200` with the updated customer. Inside the `customer` object, send only the fields you want to change. Fields you leave out keep their current values. Sending `custom_properties` replaces the customer's whole list, so include every entry you want to keep. Leave `custom_properties` out to keep the list unchanged. Send each entry as `{label, description}`. The API also accepts `{name, value}`, but the response always uses `label` and `description`. An entry keeps its `id` while its `label` and `description` stay the same; new text gets a new `id`. You can set `store_credit` directly, but the API does not record the change in the customer's store credit history. The balance can then differ from the total of the recorded adjustments. To record a change, use [Adjust store credit](/api-reference/customers/adjust-store-credit).

parameters.description: The `customer_id` of the customer to update. Do not send its `internal_id`: that number can also be another customer's `customer_id`, so the call can update the wrong customer.

delete.description: Deletes a customer and returns `204` with no body. The API moves the customer to the trash; it does not erase the record. [Retrieve a customer](/api-reference/customers/retrieve-a-customer) still returns it, with `is_in_trash: true`. Its email address stays registered: [Create a customer](/api-reference/customers/create-a-customer) rejects that address with `409`, and [Check an email address](/api-reference/customers/check-an-email-address) returns `exists: true` for it. [Export customers](/api-reference/customers/export-customers) leaves deleted customers out. You cannot restore a deleted customer through the API; use the WebCommander admin interface. Deleting the same customer again returns `404` with the message `Customer already in trash`.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: The `customer_id` of the customer to delete. Do not send its `internal_id`: that number can also be another customer's `customer_id`, so the call can delete the wrong customer.

204.description: The customer is now in the trash. The response has no body.

404.description: No customer has that `customer_id`, or the customer is already in the trash. In the second case, the message is `Customer already in trash`.

get.description: Returns an XLSX spreadsheet of your customers. The file always contains every customer except deleted ones, whatever parameters you send. The parameters choose which columns appear, not which customers. To keep a column, leave its parameter out or send `1`, `true`, `on` or `yes`. Any other value removes the column. For example, `status=active` removes the status column and still exports every customer. With no parameters, the file has 21 columns. `Customer Id`, `Gender` and `Email` are always included. post.description: Adds one or more addresses to a customer. Send them as a list in `customer.addresses`, and give each one a `type` of `primary`, `shipping` or `billing`. [Create a customer](/api-reference/customers/create-a-customer) discards any address fields you send it, so use this call to add addresses. Any other `type` is rejected with `400 invalid_enum`. A `state` that is not in the address's `country` is rejected with `400 state_country_mismatch`, and the error names the field `addresses[0].state_id`, not `state`. post.description: Queues a password reset email for each customer in `customer_ids`. Send `customer_id` values, not `internal_id`. The call is asynchronous: a `202` means the emails are queued, not that they have been sent. An id that matches no customer does not fail the call. It is returned in `skipped` as `{"customer_id": …, "reason": "not_found"}`. A call that queues nothing still returns `202`, so compare `queued` and `skipped` with the ids you sent. An empty `customer_ids` list, or an id that is not an integer, is rejected with `400 validation_failed`.

202.description: The emails are queued, not yet sent. `queued` lists the ids that were queued. `skipped` lists each id that was not, with a `reason`. `requested` is the number of ids you sent and `total_queued` is the number queued.

get.description: To get the next page, send the response's `pagination.next_page` as `page`; it is `null` when there are no more pages. Only `limit`, `offset` and `page` change the result: `sort`, an `action` filter and unknown parameters are ignored, not rejected. Entries do not include `balance_before` or `balance_after`, so save them from the [Adjust store credit](/api-reference/customers/adjust-store-credit) response each time you make an adjustment. You cannot rebuild a customer's balance from this list, because setting `store_credit` with [Update a customer](/api-reference/customers/update-a-customer) changes the balance without adding an entry.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: The customer's `customer_id` from [List customers](/api-reference/customers/list-customers). Do not send `internal_id`, because the same number can be another customer's `customer_id`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of adjustments per page, up to `20`. A larger value is not rejected: you get at most `20`, and `pagination.limit` shows `20`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of adjustments to skip. If you send both `offset` and `page`, `offset` is used and `page` is ignored.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at `1`. Each page holds `limit` adjustments, at most `20`.

200.description: Returns `store_credit_adjustments`, newest first, and `pagination`. Each adjustment has `id`, `customer_id`, `internal_id`, `action`, `amount`, `note`, `created_at` and `created_by`. `pagination` has `total`, `limit`, `offset`, `count`, `current_page`, `total_pages`, `has_next`, `has_previous`, `previous_page` and `next_page`.

post.description: Adds credit to a customer or deducts it, and records the change in their store credit history. Send `action`, `amount` and an optional `note` at the top level of the JSON body, not inside a `customer` object. `action` is `add` or `deduct` and sets the direction, so `amount` is always a positive number. Save `balance_before` and `balance_after` from the response if you need them, because [List store credit adjustments](/api-reference/customers/list-store-credit-adjustments) does not return them.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: The customer's `customer_id` from [List customers](/api-reference/customers/list-customers). Do not send `internal_id`: the same number can be another customer's `customer_id`, and that customer would get the adjustment.

201.description: Returns the saved `store_credit_adjustment` and the customer's new balance as `store_credit`, which equals `balance_after`. The adjustment has `id`, `customer_id`, `internal_id`, `action`, `amount`, `note`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `balance_before` and `balance_after`. If you did not send `note`, it is `null`.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST "$WC_BASE_URL/api/v4/admin/customers/123/store-credit/adjustments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "action": "add",
    "amount": 20,
    "note": "Refund"
  }'
